description: Annotation output format specification. Each annotated record represents one abstract with all entity mentions and relations.

entities.entity_id: string — Unique ID within this record (e.g., T1, T2, ...)
entities.type: string — Entity type: GeneOrProtein | Chemical | Disease | SequenceVariant | Pathway | CellLine
entities.text: string — Exact text span as it appears in the abstract
entities.start: int — Character offset start (0-indexed, relative to abstract field)
entities.normalized_id: string — Database identifier if available (e.g., NCBI:3845 for KRAS, MESH:D000077192 for gemcitabine). Empty string if not normalized.

relations.relation_id: string — Unique ID within this record (e.g., R1, R2, ...)
relations.type: string — Relation type: Positive_Correlation | Negative_Correlation | Association | Binding | Drug_Interaction | Cotreatment | Comparison | Conversion
relations.subject_id: string — entity_id of the subject entity (for directed relations)
relations.object_id: string — entity_id of the object entity (for directed relations)
relations.directed: boolean — true if subject→object direction is meaningful
relations.evidence_sentence: string — The sentence (or sentences) that most clearly supports this relation

metadata.annotation_time_seconds: int — Time spent annotating this record
metadata.confidence: string — high | medium | low — Annotator's confidence in the annotations
metadata.notes: string — Any annotator notes or flags

example_annotated_record.title: Saikosaponin D overcomes gemcitabine resistance in pancreatic cancer via AKT/mTOR pathway inhibition and synergistic induction of apoptosis and autophagy.
example_annotated_record.abstract: Gemcitabine (GEM) is the first-line chemotherapy drug for pancreatic cancer, but its efficacy is often limited by inherent drug resistance. Saikosaponin D (SSD), a bioactive triterpenoid saponin, exhibits antitumor properties. The present study investigated the effects of SSD on pancreatic cancer cells, and evaluated whether SSD can overcome GEM resistance.

relations.evidence_sentence: Gemcitabine (GEM) is the first-line chemotherapy drug for pancreatic cancer
evaluated whether SSD can overcome GEM resistance
SSD can overcome GEM resistance to enhance its antitumor effects
